entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Sultan Walad, born in 1299 in Konya, Anatolia (modern-day Turkey), was the eldest son of the renowned Sufi poet and mystic Rumi. He became one of the founders of the Mevlevi Order, a mystical Islamic sect known for its whirling dervishes, and played a key role in spreading its teachings throughout the Middle East and Central Asia.











Sultan Walad's significance lies in his ability to synthesize the mystical and philosophical traditions of Islam with the spiritual and artistic expressions of the Sufi Order, creating a unique and powerful spiritual movement that continues to inspire and influence people around the world today.











As a scholar and mystic, Sultan Walad was deeply influenced by the works of Ibn Arabi and other Sufi scholars, and his own writings on the nature of the self and the universe continue to be studied and revered by scholars and practitioners of Sufism to this day.











His legacy extends far beyond the Mevlevi Order, however, as Sultan Walad's teachings and writings have had a profound impact on the development of Islamic mysticism and the spiritual traditions of the Middle East and Central Asia.
